text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Jails in eastern Denmark are now kept under police surveillance to prevent new attacks on prisons where bikers are in custody for offences in the ongoing biker war between Hells Angels and Bandidos.

--- Over the past 12 months the Danish windmill industry has sold a record of 1,300 windmills with a total capacity of 600 Megawatts, corresponding to the total number of windmills installed in Denmark within the last 15 years or Sweden's Barseback nuclear power station.

--- Financial regulations in other European Union countries may slow down economic growth in Denmark next year and growth and employment may therefore not be as good as expected a former member of the Denmark's Economic Council, the "wise men" says.
--- Although the latest SAS strike in Copenhagen airport has now ended, new conflicts could arise, as 1,300 airport employees are very discontented with new management pension proposals.
--- The European commission is delaying a Danish bill on electricity liberalisation suspecting that Denmark seeks to protect large power stations from competition.
